1 J U D G M E N T / AWAR D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land LAC no.
367 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Pravin Kumar v. Union of India Page no. 2 of 12 with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".

entities.text: Pravin Kumar v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 6/22/2 (10), 8/2 (416), 9 (416), 11 (4 16), 12 Min (118), 15/7 min (208), 29/20/1 (15), 30/1/8 (413), 25 min (1151/2), 33/16 (4 16), 25 min (22), 34/11 Min (104), 20 (416) i.e. total area 40 bigha 51/2 biswas situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
LAC no. 367 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Pravin Kumar v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 12 5.

sentences.text:
It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been arbitrarily assessed by the LAC without taking into account the fertility, potentiality,
surroundings and topography under acquisition.

The said land is levelled land and is situated in a belt which has not experienced any major earthquake, flood or any other natural calamity for the last more than hundred years and is best suited for all sorts of land uses like residential,
commercial, industrial and agricultural etc.
the quality of the said land makes it most suitable in the state of Delhi.

sentences.text: It is stated that the said land falls in the most fertile belt of Delhi and the petitioners are cultivating the said land and are growing three crops in a year "fasali year".

Whole of the said land is having welldeveloped irrigation system having borwell, tubewells and canal system linked with Yamuna Canal and all crops including cereals, vegetables crops, oil yielding crops and sugarcane are being cultivated by the petitioners and the income per acre is more than Rs. 2 lakhs per year.
In addition to it, the petitioners are having milk yielding cattles which are fully fed by the land produce and all the daily needs of the petitioners are fulfilled by the said land.

7. It is stated that the petitioners shall be forced to change from one mode of life i.e. agro based lifestyle to modern lifestyle due to the LAC no. 367 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Pravin Kumar v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 12 acquisition of the said land and the new lifestyle has become more expensive, and the daily inflation shall have an adverse economic effect on the petitioners, who were selfreliant before acquisition of the said land.

entities.text: Pravin Kumar v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said land acquired by the ld. LAC is surrounded by the residential as well as industrial areas.
The area under acquisition is having mettled roads, and is having a very good connectivity with other areas of Delhi.
The National Highway10 is just 1 km away from the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera and the railway line from Delhi Junction to Firozpur is just half kilometres away.

The infrastructure in the vicinity of the land of the petitioners is already in existence i.e. electricity, schools, residential areas and industrial areas, have been developed which has enhanced the market value of the said land.

8. It is stated that the land under acquisition including the said land is having better location than the revenue estate of Village like Karala, Savda, Madanpur Dabas, Mundaka, Ghewra and Hiran Koodna, etc which falls on the NorthWestern and SouthWestern side of the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi where sale instances show constant rise in the land rates, however,
those lands are far away from village Rani Khera, if the distance from the urban limits of Delhi state are taken into consideration.

The said land has great potentiality and is fit for supporting high rise buildings, and other residential infrastructure with a lesser investment, if compared with the development work carried out in South Delhi and East Delhi, where the land was hilly, terrain and low line LAC no. 367 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Pravin Kumar v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 12 respectively, which require a huge amount for levelling and making the land usable for construction activities.

entities.text: Pravin Kumar v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The ld. LAC has overlooked the facts while determining the market value of the said land, in as much as, if all the factors are taken together for assessing the market value of the land under acquisition, it shall be Rs. 1 crore per acre or at least Rs. 2000/ per square yard.

If the said land under acquisition is auctioned to the private developers, they would have purchased the same for more than Rs. 1 crore per acre, which fact finds support from the fact that the land bordering Delhi, particularly in the village Kundli and Kasar in Haryana, has shown a very fast increase in the land prices due to participation of private builders, however, the land of Village Kundli and Kasar is comparatively inferior to the land under acquisition.

9. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming market value of Rs. 2000/ per sq. yards or Rs. 1 crores per acre in addition to the said market value.
The petitioners have also claimed solatium @ 30% and additional amount @ 12% and further claim interest @ 9% and 15% as per the provisions of the Act.

sentences.text: Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the petition as framed, is not maintainable as the petitioner has failed to furnish any evidence in respect of the relief claimed in the present petition and as such merits dismissal.

The LAC has already LAC no. 367 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Pravin Kumar v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 12 assessed the market value of the land in question taking into consideration the prevailing market rates of the land at the time of notification under Section 4 of the LA Act.

sentences.text: All the other averments made in the petition was denied in toto and it has been submitted that the reference filed by the petitioner is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed.

It is submitted that the reference petition is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed as no ground or reason has been shown by the petitioners for enhancement in the market value of the land which were correctly assessed by the learned LAC.

11. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Mubarakpur Dabas had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

12. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest LAC no. 367 / 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Pravin Kumar v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 12 on the delayed period.

entities.text: Pravin Kumar v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
13. It is stated that the possession of the said land has been taken over by the DDA on 04.04.2006 and after taking possession, the same has been transferred to RPDVII.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action, therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is level to be dismissed with cost.
14.
On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 01.04.2015:  ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?

18. To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Savitri Devi (supra).

20. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value as awarded in the case of Savitri Devi (supra) in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

21. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
